items.title: PESTLE is a checklist, not a model
items.claim: PESTLE analysis covers Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors. What is its main analytical limitation?

options.text: It can predict the future with high accuracy
It generates an inventory of factors but does not weight them, link them or model their interactions — students often produce long unprioritised lists
It is legally required for UK firms
It only applies to large firms

items.reveal_title: A scanning tool, not a strategy
items.reveal:
PESTLE (originally PEST, expanded over time) traces to Francis Aguilar's 'Scanning the Business Environment' (1967). It's a structured way to spot environmental change but provides no mechanism to prioritise or combine factors.

Scenario planning (Royal Dutch Shell, from Pierre Wack in the 1970s) goes further: it builds plausible coherent futures and tests strategy against them. PESTLE feeds into scenario planning, not the other way around.
items.why: PESTLE is useful for ensuring you haven't missed an external factor. It's not a strategy tool on its own.

items.title: COVID exposed how thin most supply chains were
items.claim: During 2020-22, automotive production was held back by shortages of one component category in particular. Which was it?

options.text: Semiconductors (chips) — the global shortage cost the automotive industry an estimated $210 billion in lost revenue in 2021 alone (AlixPartners)

items.reveal:
When auto demand fell in spring 2020, car makers cancelled chip orders. Foundries (TSMC, Samsung) reallocated capacity to consumer electronics, where demand was surging. When car demand returned, chip capacity was booked out. Ford alone lost around 1.25 million units of production in 2021.

The US CHIPS Act (2022) and EU Chips Act (2023) responded with $50bn+ in subsidies for domestic semiconductor manufacturing — a direct strategic response to the disruption.
items.why: Multi-tier supply chains hide concentration risk. A car maker can have hundreds of direct suppliers but still depend on two or three foundries for chips.

items.title: Depreciation methods change reported profit, not cash
items.claim: A delivery van costs £40,000 with a 4-year useful life and £8,000 residual value. Under straight-line depreciation, what is the year-1 depreciation charge?
items.reveal_title: Straight-line: (cost minus residual) divided by life
items.reveal:
(£40,000 - £8,000) / 4 = £8,000 per year. Reducing balance would front-load the charge (e.g. 40% of £40,000 = £16,000 in year 1).

Neither method affects cash flow — the van was paid for upfront. Depreciation is an accounting allocation that matches cost to revenue across periods, governed by IAS 16. Different methods produce different reported profits in early years but the same total over the asset's life.
items.why: Profit figures are sensitive to accounting policy choices. Cash flow is not. This is one reason cash flow statements were made mandatory under IAS 7.
